fact: In standard tennis scoring, points progress from Love (0) to 15, then 30, then 40, before winning game point.
The four Grand Slam tournaments in tennis are the Australian Open, French Open (Roland Garros), Wimbledon, and the US Open.
Rafael Nadal is known as the 'King of Clay' after winning an unprecedented 14 French Open men's singles titles.
Wimbledon is the only Grand Slam tournament played on natural grass courts.
Novak Djokovic holds the men's all-time record for the most Grand Slam singles titles in the Open Era with 24 titles.
Serena Williams won 23 Grand Slam singles titles in the Open Era, the most by any player in the modern era.
The longest match in professional tennis history was played at Wimbledon 2010 between John Isner and Nicolas Mahut, lasting 11 hours and 5 minutes across three days.
The height of a tennis net is standard at exactly 3 feet (0.914 meters) at the center strap and 3.5 feet (1.07 meters) at the posts.
Steffi Graf achieved the only 'Golden Slam' in tennis history in 1988, winning all four Grand Slam titles and the Olympic Singles Gold medal in the same calendar year.
Roger Federer holds the record for the most consecutive weeks ranked as World No. 1 in ATP history with 237 consecutive weeks from 2004 to 2008.
The 'Open Era' of professional tennis began in 1968, when Grand Slam tournaments allowed professional players to compete alongside amateurs.
In a standard tiebreak game at 6-6 in a set, the first player or team to reach 7 points with a margin of at least 2 points wins the set.
Sam Groth of Australia hit the fastest officially recorded serve in tennis history at 163.7 mph (263.4 km/h) at a Busan Challenger event in 2012.
Spencer Gore won the inaugural Wimbledon Championships in 1877, defeating William Marshall in 48 minutes with a score of 6-1, 6-2, 6-4.
Margaret Court holds the all-time record across both amateur and Open Eras with 24 Grand Slam singles titles and 64 major titles overall.
A 'Golden Set' in tennis occurs when a player wins a set 6-0 without dropping a single point (winning all 24 consecutive points), achieved by Yaroslava Shvedova at Wimbledon 2012.
The French Open (Roland Garros) is named after the French aviator and World War I hero Roland Garros, who was the first person to fly across the Mediterranean.
Goran Ivanisevic is the only player in tennis history to win a Wimbledon men's singles title entering the tournament as a wildcard, accomplishing the feat in 2001.
